{"status": "success", "summary": "Implemented all three independent module skeletons; each is an Impl method.

Files changed (tests untouched):
- measure.py — Impl.to_cm(value, unit): factor map {m:100, cm:1, mm:0.1}; returns int(round(value*factor)); unknown unit raises ValueError.
- slugify.py — Impl.slugify(text): lowercases, re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "-", ...), strips leading/trailing "-", returns "untitled" when empty.
- ranges.py — Impl.merge(ranges): sorts by start, merges overlapping intervals only (start <= current end), returns list of tuples.

Note: the prose spec said "adjacent or overlapping", but the authoritative test expects [1,3],[2,4],[5,7] -> [(1,4),(5,7)], i.e. touching-but-not-overlapping intervals stay separate. I followed the tests (adjacent-end+1 merging was tried first and failed the test).

Commands actually run:
- `python -m pytest -q` — first run: 1 failed (test_ranges, because I initially merged adjacent ranges), 2 passed.
- After fixing ranges.py to overlap-only: `python -m pytest -q` -> "3 passed in 0.01s".
- Manual edge checks: to_cm(0.1,'m')=10, to_cm(2.54,'cm')=3, to_cm(7,'mm')=1, invalid 'FT' -> ValueError; slugify("Hello, World!")="hello-world", slugify("  --A@@B-- ")="a-b", slugify("***")="untitled", slugify("Foo---BAR_baz")="foo-bar-baz"; merge([[5,7],[1,3],[2,4]])=[(1,4),(5,7)], merge([])=[], merge([[1,1]])=[(1,1)], merge([[1,2],[3,4],[10,10],[11,12]]) — non-overlapping ranges preserved.", "evidence": ["measure.py, slugify.py, ranges.py written", "python -m pytest -q => 3 passed in 0.01s", "manual python -c edge checks output: cm 10 3 1; ValueError ok; slug hello-world a-b untitled foo-bar-baz; extra merge [(1,2),(3,4),(10,10),(11,12)]"], "unverified": ["Prose requirement that adjacent (touching) intervals merge conflicts with tests/test_ranges.py; implemented overlap-only per the test. Not implemented as literally stated in the prose."]}
